card.summary: H.R. 7748, the Railway Safety Act of 2026, aims to enhance safety requirements for trains transporting hazardous materials and improve overall rail safety. The bill mandates safety standards for high-hazard trains, establishes minimum crew sizes for freight trains, requires advanced defect detection systems and enhanced track and equipment inspections, increases penalties for rail safety violations, and provides grants and emergency response programs for hazardous materials preparedness.
card.title: Railway Safety Act of 2026

latest_action.text: Referred to the Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Railway Safety Act of 2026 establishes new safety requirements for trains carrying hazardous materials, mandates minimum freight train crew sizes, updates inspection and defect detection rules, increases civil penalties for rail safety violations, and provides funding for emergency response and preparedness grants.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with new safety, crew size, inspection, defect detection, and emergency preparedness requirements, and face higher financial penalties for violations.

Guaranteed minimum two-person crew sizes for most freight trains, subjected to mandatory breath or body fluid testing for equipment inspectors, and protected from limits on time required for safety inspections.
Receive enhanced hazardous materials training opportunities, grants, personal protective equipment funding, and access to real-time train consist information and commodity flow reports.
Subject to annual registration fees ranging from $250 to $5,000 depending on small business status to fund emergency preparedness.

key_provisions: Requires Class I railroads operating high-hazard trains to generate electronic train consist information, share commodity flow reports with state and tribal emergency response commissions, and submit emergency response plans.
Mandates that freight trains operated by a Class I railroad must be operated by a minimum of a 2-person crew consisting of a conductor and a locomotive engineer, with certain exceptions.
Increases maximum civil penalties for railroad safety violations up to $1,000,000 normally, and up to $5,000,000 for violations resulting in death, serious injury, or substantial property damage.
Phases out older tank cars transporting Class 3 flammable liquids by December 31, 2027, unless they meet DOT-117, DOT-117P, or DOT-117R specifications.
Directs the Secretary of Transportation to issue regulations requiring risk-based defect detector network plans from Class I railroads.
Requires railroad carriers to establish a toll-free telephone service to directly receive calls reporting blocked highway-rail grade crossings.
Establishes an emergency response assistance program to provide immediate financial assistance to communities responding to significant hazardous materials transportation incidents.
missing_information: The total net cost to the federal government and private industry for implementing all mandated studies, grants, and technology upgrades is not fully specified, as several authorizations leave amounts to 'such sums as may be necessary'.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Railway Safety Act of 2026 establishes new safety requirements for trains carrying hazardous materials, mandates minimum freight train crew sizes, updates inspection and defect detection rules, increases civil penalties for rail safety violations, and provides funding for emergency response and preparedness grants.
summary_detail.significance: The Railway Safety Act of 2026 represents a substantial federal intervention in freight and hazardous materials rail transportation, significantly modifying operating rules, equipment standards, and emergency response funding.
